mechanism_narrative: The weekly RETAIL_REC series has improved from -86.3 to -81.1 and GROCERY_PHARM from -48.1 to -39.0 over the last four weeks; this persistent adaptation to pandemic conditions will continue, causing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks to be higher than its last-four-week mean.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT mobility crosses above -75.0 for two consecutive weeks, it signals that government restrictions have eased enough for commuting to resume, which will pull RETAIL_REC higher over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean rises above -75.0 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: After TRANSIT exceeds -75.0 for two consecutive weeks, the next two-week mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the preceding two-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: Joint increases in PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM reflect outdoor social activity and household restocking; this combined behavior will spill over into retail-and-recreation visits, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: When PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both rise week-on-week, the next two-week mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the prior two-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: In an early-reopening regime, a fall in RESIDENTIAL below 25.0 combined with WORKPLACES rising above -66.0 signals that people are leaving home for work, which increases retail-and-recreation footfall over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below 25.0 and WORKPLACES weekly mean rises above -66.0
failure_condition: Under early reopening, when RESIDENTIAL is below 25.0 and WORKPLACES is above -66.0, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Late-spring weather and the approach of Memorial Day weekend increase park visits; the observed PARKS improvement from -67.1 to -51.3 will coincide with more retail-and-recreation trips over the next week.
failure_condition: In the next week, RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the current week despite PARKS remaining above -55.0.

mechanism_narrative: The steady rise in WORKPLACES from -69.6 to -65.3 indicates that office commuting is slowly returning; this commuting recovery will translate into higher retail-and-recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the mean over the last 28 days when WORKPLACES has improved for four consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently high RESIDENTIAL above 24.5 combined with TRANSIT remaining below -76 signals continued avoidance of public spaces; this behavioral caution will cause RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks to fall below its last-four-week mean.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 24.5 and TRANSIT stays below -76.0
failure_condition: When RESIDENTIAL is above 24.5 and TRANSIT is below -76.0, the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is higher than or equal to the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A week-over-week improvement in TRANSIT of more than 2 points indicates that policy easing is taking effect; this will produce a near-term increase in RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean improves by more than 2.0 points week-over-week
failure_condition: After a TRANSIT week-over-week improvement greater than 2.0 points, the next week's RETAIL_REC is not higher than the current week's RETAIL_REC.
